svg.title: Celery event-driven architecture
svg.desc: Event-driven architecture for Celery: producer applications serialize task requests into messages and publish to a broker queue; worker consumers asynchronously receive and execute tasks; results stored in result backend; workers also react to scheduled events, retries, revokes, and lifecycle events. Producers and workers are fully decoupled.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does a Django application call a Celery task?')
sendPrompt('How does a CLI script trigger a Celery task?')
sendPrompt('How does Celery Beat produce scheduled task events?')

svg.text: serialize task → message · publish to broker queue

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the Celery message broker decouple producers from workers?')
g.text: RabbitMQ · Redis · Amazon SQS · Kafka — task queues · routing keys · priorities
Worker consumers — react to task events
Producer never calls worker execution logic directly

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does a Celery worker receive and execute a task?')
sendPrompt('Can multiple Celery workers process tasks concurrently?')
sendPrompt('How do Celery workers scale horizontally?')

svg.text: Workers also react to: retry events · revoke events · time-limit events · result updates · worker lifecycle events

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the Celery result backend store task outcomes?')
g.text: Redis · database · Amazon S3 — store task state, return value, and errors

svg.text: Producers and workers fully decoupled — work triggered by asynchronous messages, not direct request-response chains
